name: Pouch
description:
A cloth or leather pouch can hold up to 20 sling bullets or 50 blowgun needles, among other things. A compartmentalized pouch for holding spell components is called a component pouch (described earlier in this section).
Capacity: 1/5 cubic foot/6 pounds of gear.

name: Purple worm poison
description:
This poison must be harvested from a dead or incapacitated purple worm. A creature subjected to this poison must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw, taking 42 (12d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
\n\n
**_Injury._** Injury poison can be applied to weapons, ammunition, trap components, and other objects that deal piercing or slashing damage and remains potent until delivered through a wound or washed off. A creature that takes piercing or slashing damage from an object coated with the poison is exposed to its effects.

name: Quarterstaff
description: A quarterstaff.

name: Quiver
description: A quiver can hold up to 20 arrows.

name: Ram, Portable
description: You can use a portable ram to break down doors. When doing so, you gain a +4 bonus on the Strength check. One other character can help you use the ram, giving you advantage on this check.

name: Rapier
description: A rapier.

name: Rations (1 day)
description: Rations consist of dry foods suitable for extended travel, including jerky, dried fruit, hardtack, and nuts.

name: Reliquary
description: Can be used as a holy symbol.

name: Ring mail
description: This armor is leather armor with heavy rings sewn into it. The rings help reinforce the armor against blows from swords and axes. Ring mail is inferior to chain mail, and it's usually worn only by those who can't afford better armor.

name: Robes
description: Robes, for wearing.

name: Rod
description: Can be used as an arcane focus.

name: Rope, hempen (50 feet)
description: Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

name: Rope, silk (50 feet)
description: Rope, whether made of hemp or silk, has 2 hit points and can be burst with a DC 17 Strength check.

name: Rowboat
description: Waterborne vehicle. Speed 1.5mph

name: Sack
description: A sack. Capacity: 1 cubic foot/30 pounds of gear.

name: Saffron
description: 1lb of saffron.

name: Sailing Ship
description: Waterborne vehicle. Speed 2mph

name: Salt
description: 1lb of salt.

name: Scale mail
description: This armor consists of a coat and leggings (and perhaps a separate skirt) of leather covered with overlapping pieces of metal, much like the scales of a fish. The suit includes gauntlets.

name: Scale, Merchant's
description: A scale includes a small balance, pans, and a suitable assortment of weights up to 2 pounds. With it, you can measure the exact weight of small objects, such as raw precious metals or trade goods, to help determine their worth.

name: Scimitar
description: A scimitar.

name: Sealing wax
description: For sealing written letters.

name: Serpent venom
description:
This poison must be harvested from a dead or incapacitated giant poisonous snake. A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw, taking 10 (3d6) poison damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
\n\n
**_Injury._** Injury poison can be applied to weapons, ammunition, trap components, and other objects that deal piercing or slashing damage and remains potent until delivered through a wound or washed off. A creature that takes piercing or slashing damage from an object coated with the poison is exposed to its effects.

name: Shawm
description: Several of the most common types of musical instruments are shown on the table as examples. If you have proficiency with a given musical instrument, you can add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to play music with the instrument. A bard can use a musical instrument as a spellcasting focus. Each type of musical instrument requires a separate proficiency.

name: Sheep
description: One sheep.

name: Shield
description: A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.

name: Shortbow
description: A shortbow

name: Shortsword
description: A short sword.

name: Shovel
description: A shovel.

name: Sickle
description: A sickle.

name: Signal whistle
description: For signalling.

name: Signet Ring
description: A ring with a signet on it.

name: Silk
description: 1 sq. yd. of silk.

name: Silver
description: 1lb of silver

name: Silver Piece
description: One gold piece is worth ten silver pieces, the most prevalent coin among commoners. A silver piece buys a laborer's work for half a day, a flask of lamp oil, or a night's rest in a poor inn.

name: Sled
description: Drawn vehicle

name: Sling
description: A sling.

name: Sling bullets
description: Technically their cost is 20 for 4cp.

name: Smith's tools
description:
These special tools include the items needed to pursue a craft or trade.\n\n
Proficiency with a set of artisan’s tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make using the tools in your craft. Each type of artisan’s tools requires a separate proficiency.

name: Soap
description: For cleaning.

name: Spear
description: A spear.

name: Spellbook
description: Essential for wizards, a spellbook is a leather-­‐‑bound tome with 100 blank vellum pages suitable for recording spells.

name: Spike, iron
description: An iron spike.

name: Splint Armor
description: This armor is made of narrow vertical strips of metal riveted to a backing of leather that is worn over cloth padding. Flexible chain mail protects the joints.

name: Sprig of mistletoe
description: A sprig of mistletoe that can be used as a druidic focus.

name: Spyglass
description: Objects viewed through a spyglass are magnified to twice their size.

name: Staff
description: Can be used as an arcane focus.

name: Studded Leather Armor
description: Made from tough but flexible leather, studded leather is reinforced with close-set rivets or spikes.

name: Tent
description: A simple and portable canvas shelter, a tent sleeps two.

name: Thieves' tools
description: This set of tools includes a small file, a set of lock picks, a small mirror mounted on a metal handle, a set of narrow-­‐‑bladed scissors, and a pair of pliers. Proficiency with these tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make to disarm traps or open locks.

name: Tinderbox
description: This small container holds flint, fire steel, and tinder (usually dry cloth soaked in light oil) used to kindle a fire. Using it to light a torch—or anything else with abundant, exposed fuel—takes an action. Lighting any other fire takes 1 minute.

name: Tinker's tools
description:
These special tools include the items needed to pursue a craft or trade.\n\n
Proficiency with a set of artisan’s tools lets you add your proficiency bonus to any ability checks you make using the tools in your craft. Each type of artisan’s tools requires a separate proficiency.

name: Torch
description: A torch burns for 1 hour, providing bright light in a 20-­‐‑foot radius and dim light for an additional 20 feet. If you make a melee attack with a burning torch and hit, it deals 1 fire damage.

name: Torpor
description:
A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 4d6 hours. The poisoned creature is incapacitated.
\n\n
**_Ingested._** A creature must swallow an entire dose of ingested poison to suffer its effects. The dose can be delivered in food or a liquid. You may decide that a partial dose has a reduced effect, such as allowing advantage on the saving throw or dealing only half damage on a failed save.

name: Totem
description: Can be used as a druidic focus.

name: Trident

name: Truth serum
description:
A creature subjected to this poison must succeed on a DC 11 Constitution saving throw or become poisoned for 1 hour. The poisoned creature can't knowingly speak a lie, as if under the effect of a zone of truth spell.
\n\n
**_Ingested._** A creature must swallow an entire dose of ingested poison to suffer its effects. The dose can be delivered in food or a liquid. You may decide that a partial dose has a reduced effect, such as allowing advantage on the saving throw or dealing only half damage on a failed save.
